newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND IN TROUBLE AT LUNCH ON 3RD DAY VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND IN TROUBLE AT LUNCH ON 3RD DAY VS NZ.

text.p: England were in trouble at lunch on the third day of the third and final cricket test against New Zealand at Lancaster Park on Sunday.
Replying to New Zealand's first innings 346, England were 210 for eight at lunch, with captain Mike Atherton playing a defiant lone hand to be 92 not out at the interval.
The tourists began the day at 145 for five, but lost fast-medium bowler Dominic Cork to a rash stroke on the fifth ball of the day.
Robert Croft helped Atherton add 53 in 84 minutes for the seventh wicket before Croft miscued a slow thigh-high full toss from medium pacer Nathan Astle and gave a catch to mid on.
Darren Gough was bowled by teenage left arm spinner Daniel Vettori as New Zealand worked their way through England's lower order.
At lunch Andrew Caddick was on four, and looking to help his captain through to his 11th test hundred.
Atherton had batted 323 minutes, faced 221 balls and hit 10 boundaries in an innings notable for some handsome drives, vigorous pull and hook strokes and plenty of concentration.
Left armer Geoff Allott had taken three for 64, Astle two for 26 with one wicket apiece to Chris Cairns, Vettori and Heath Davis.
New Zealand need to win the test to square the series after England won the second test by an innings and 68 runs at Wellington.
